## Summary

Nuclear deformation can influence both the initial geometry and final-state observables
in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. This presentation explored an additional aspect of
nuclear structure: **shape coexistence**, in which a nucleus can exhibit multiple
competing geometric configurations.

Using a Glauber-model description of the collision geometry, the study investigated how
shape coexistence modifies initial-state observables relevant for heavy-ion collisions,
including eccentricity and transverse-area fluctuations. The work provided an early step
toward connecting nuclear-structure information from low-energy measurements with
observables accessible in relativistic nuclear collisions.
